questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A given mass of gas occupies 400 cm³ at a pressure of 760 mmHg. What volume will it occupy at 380 mmHg if the temperature remains constant?
questions.explanation: By Boyle's Law (P1V1 = P2V2 at constant temperature): 760 * 400 = 380 * V2 => V2 = (760 * 400) / 380 = 800 cm³.
questions.explanation_pidgin: Since pressure drop by half from 760 to 380 mmHg, volume go double from 400 cm³ to 800 cm³.
